summary: Six consumer advocates ask FERC to rehear its order accepting PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement. They challenge four elements: pay-as-bid market power, the $555/MW-day cap, the 15-year term and the lack of locational limits.
ask: Grant rehearing, find the four identified RBP elements unjust and unreasonable, and direct PJM to change them in any later FPA section 205 filing.

points.point: The advocates call the pay-as-bid design flawed because it permits seller-side market power and likely over-procures at high cost.
points.quote: it permits the unmitigated exercise of seller-side market power and its design seems guaranteed to ensure that PJM procures more resources than are necessary, at costs higher than are warranted.

points.point: The $555/MW-day cap is borrowed from a 2028/2029 BRA reference point that was replaced by a $325/MW-day collar, and would apply for up to 15 years.
points.quote: price cap that is 70% higher and will be applied to commitment periods up to 15 times longer than was the case for the 2028/2029 BRA.

points.point: They say the 15-year commitment could add about $13 billion of unneeded cost, since PJM says five years addresses the shortfall.
points.quote: could unjustly and unreasonably saddle captive ratepayers with some $13 billion in excessive and unnecessary RBP costs.

points.point: They say the Order does not engage the objection that the RBP has no locational constraints, noting up to 6,831 MW against 149 GW of existing supply.
points.quote: the volume of capacity that PJM will procure through the RBP auction— up to 6,831 MW—is relatively small compared with total existing supply in PJM

points.point: Resources chosen without regard to location could dilute BRA locational price signals for up to 15 years.
points.quote: those resources will participate in the BRA as price takers and will thereby diminish the effect of the BRA’s locational price signals for up to 15 years.

points.point: Relief requested: rehearing, a finding that four RBP elements are unjust and unreasonable, and directed changes in a later filing.
points.quote: find unjust and unreasonable the four elements of the RBP framework identified herein by Joint Consumer Advocates; and (3) direct PJM to incorporate changes to those elements

throughLine.text: Challenges who pays for PJM's backstop capacity procurement in ER26-3380, a supply-side track running beside the E-7 show cause order, whose adequacy report and cost-recovery directive address large-load cost responsibility.
